source.title: Detecting noisy labels using checkpoint ensembles

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures noisy-label learning dynamics through detection performance across training checkpoints, using a different measure from the original memorization studies.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior findings about clean-priority learning, but those cited results are not this study's evidence. Its own temporal results concern detection of corrupted labels; it does not report fitting a fully random labeling or training error on random labels.
record.test_reason: Section 6 reports the transition from early generalization to later memorization in ordinary SGD training. Prediction-based noise-detection recall is the fraction of corrupted training labels still misclassified, so its decline directly measures increased fitting of those labels. Together with the reported classification dynamics, this bears on V6; the detector benchmarks alone do not.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: carefully selected checkpoint ensembles provide competitive noisy-label detection and filtered-training performance, while scheduler and checkpoint choices materially affect detection quality. No method variant is universally best.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses ResNet-18 classification with synthetic label corruption and measures noisy-label detection across checkpoints; it does not reproduce a full random-label fitting experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The learning-rate scheduler changes the relationship between early stopping, generalization, memorization, and noise-detection performance; the authors report that recall declines after early stopping for the tested schedulers.

fits_no_version.finding: BGSS gradient-sign separation and its noise-detection recall measure detector performance rather than the order in which clean and noisy labels are fitted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clean and noisy samples can exhibit distinguishable feature-bias gradient statistics useful for label-noise detection.

record.problems: The cited temporal result is described in text but its numerical values are figure-only. The empirical evaluation reports a single run per setup. The study measures noisy-label detection rather than training error on a fully random labeling.
record.rows_left_out: No other own result directly measures whether true-label patterns are learned before random labels. Results in Tables 1–9 concern noisy-label detection or filtered-training performance, not the fitting behavior named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Completely random training labels, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily degrading test performance across corruption fractions from zero to all.
Effects of adding or removing explicit regularization on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Fully random labeling and generality beyond the reported architecture, datasets, and training schedules.

missing.what: Record the underlying training and test classification trajectories alongside prediction-based recall for each scheduler. Section 6 reports later memorization of the training set and a smooth generalization-to-memorization transition for continuous schedules versus a clearer turning point for multistep scheduling. These contextualize learning order; exact plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: Scheduler dependence of detection quality does not itself limit V6: the reported schedules differ in transition shape and checkpoint alignment, not in an explicitly reversed learning order. Each setup uses a single run.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment completely randomizes all training labels or reports zero or near-zero training error and chance test error under unchanged settings.
No comparison of training time to fit true versus random labels, or convergence time across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.
The paper tests noise-detection metrics at selected synthetic noise rates, but does not report perfect training fit and test error across a sweep from zero to all labels corrupted.
No test of whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent random-label fitting, or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
The study examines corrupted labels and checkpoint detection dynamics, not a fully random labeling or a direct comparison of fitting true labels against random labels.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measured noisy-label detection recall at model checkpoints over training.
rows.note: The authors state that recall dramatically decreases after the early stopping point for both detection methods as memorization makes more training examples correctly classified; the plotted values are not given in text.
rows.check: Split this combined row by detector and scheduler. Prediction-based recall directly measures failure to fit corrupted labels; BGSS recall measures a gradient-sign detector's performance and cannot independently establish learning order. The text explicitly reports later memorization, but exact curve values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

source_check.problem: The row combines detectors and schedulers. The qualitative observation is supported, but BGSS recall alone does not measure fitting of corrupted labels.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 with 20% uniform label noise under multistep, linear, and restarted cosine schedules
relationships.reason: R1's prediction-recall decline indicates later fitting of corrupted labels; Section 6 explicitly describes early generalization followed by memorization. This is qualitative evidence from the text, with classification trajectories missing from the record.
relationships.display_finding: Prediction recall declined later in training, indicating corrupted-label fitting after early generalization across the tested learning-rate schedules.
